messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: control-plane high 5xx/error-rate detected for multiple endpoints (auth/org-lookup/billing). Threshold breached: 7.8% 5xx over 3m across us-east-1. Paging on-call @sre_oncall. Please acknowledge and triage.

pagerduty-bot: on-call acknowledged by sre_oncall at 2026-03-15T03:14:55Z — escalation suspended.

sre_oncall: seeing similar alerts in Wavefront and a spike in analytics-ingress errors. jumping in. any customer-facing impact reported yet? cc @cs_triage_bot

nina: CS dashboard showing a rise in support chats referencing "requests failing" and recent spike in app errors for org queries. A handful of customers reporting 502s. No billing complaints yet.

lee: I can take runtime traces. quick check: increasing 502/504 from control-plane -> auth and control-plane -> org-lookup. Could be dep fanout.

sam: grabbing the control-plane logs now. Top-level stack shows a bunch of gateway errors: `upstream returned 502` and repeated `context deadline exceeded` on calls to org-lookup.

mike: Deploy bot: No recent control-plane deploys in last 30m. Last deploy was 40m ago.

sre_oncall: Runbook check: follow controlplane-dep-failure playbook — step 1: identify failing dependency. step 2: try fallback routing to cache / reduced fanout. step 3: if persists, scale or cut non-critical calls.

nina: tagging product teams — @product_ops this is affecting org-related features for some customers. ETA for comms?

product_ops: preparing a short status message for affected customers. hold until we have mitigation plan.

lee: quick query from wavefront: `sum(rate(controlplane.http.5xx[1m])) by (downstream)`. Auth service accounts for ~62% of 5xx, org-lookup ~28%, billing ~8%. Auth latency is also climbing.

sam: attaching a snippet of the control-plane proxy logs:

```
[03:12:11] PROXY upstream auth.myinfra.svc:502 "bad gateway"
[03:12:12] PROXY org-lookup.svc:504 "deadline exceeded"
[03:12:12] PROXY auth.myinfra.svc:502 "connection reset"
```

mike: looks like auth is the primary failure point. Could be heartbeat storm or a cache expiry. Any config changes to auth recently?

lee: no config pushes in last 2h. But noticed high number of parallel auth requests from the control-plane after a cache invalidation event ~03:10. Might be cache TTL too low or a regen loop.

cs_triage_bot: Affected customers (in last 10m): 12 accounts with elevated error rates, 3 with >10% failure. Customer IDs anonymized in private channel.

sre_oncall: Immediate mitigation attempt: enable degraded routing — route auth calls to read-only auth cache and reduce fanout. Initiating now, will post results.

lee: Executed a temporary cache-hot-path: `SET controlplane.auth.force_cache=true` on prod flags. Watch metrics.

sam: within 60s I see 5xx rate drop from 7.8% -> 3.2%. latency started to come down. Good signal.

nina: CS: starting proactive outreach to the three worst-hit customers. Sending templated note: "We're investigating intermittent 5xx on org lookups; limited impact; working on mitigation."

mike: however auth service still has sporadic 502 bursts. I can scale auth pool x2 as next step. anyone object?

sre_oncall: go ahead. scale auth instances + warm caches. Also enable circuit breakers on control-plane for billing calls to prevent cascade.

sam: scaling auth group now. Patch applied to autoscaler; instances reported healthy within 90s.

lee: note: metrics show a second hotspot — org-lookup downstream to the database showing increased connection wait times. Might be DB-side saturation following cache misses.

sre_oncall: contact DB oncall? we might need a short read-only failover or increase connection pool.

mike: DB oncall pinged via PD. awaiting response. In the meantime, apply a short-term throttle on org-lookup fanout to reduce pressure.

product_ops: recommended comms: "Mitigation in progress — reduced error rates observed; scaling and routing changes applied. We'll provide an update in 30 minutes." Approve? :thumbsup:

nina: approved. Sending now.

cs_triage_bot: Outbound message sent to affected customers. Template attached in private.

sre_oncall: after scaling + cache flag, 5xx down to 1.1% and customer error reports decreasing. Keeping the mitigation in place while we root-cause.

lee: interesting log pattern: control-plane is retrying certain org-lookup calls with exponential backoff disabled. There's a client-side aggressive retry flood when responses slow, amplifying load. We should re-enable backoff.

sam: found config snippet in control-plane configmap: `retry_policy: aggressive` — looks like a stale override. Rolling a quick patch to set `retry_policy: conservative` in staging then prod.

mike: patch applied and pushed; control-plane picked it up automatically. Observed immediate reduction in retry rate.

sre_oncall: nice. That likely explains the cascade: cache eviction -> retries -> DB saturation -> more 5xx. Root cause chain identified.

product_ops: timeline draft for postmortem: note cache TTL regen + aggressive retry config + DB connection pressure = cascading 5xx affecting auth/org-lookup. Recommend follow-ups: make retry conservative by default, add circuit-breaker thresholds, add cache warming on TTL expiry, DB pool monitoring alert.

nina: CS follow-up: customers who saw >10% failures will get personalized notes and a post-incident summary once RCA complete.

sre_oncall: handoff plan: I'll keep the channel open for 30m. After that, hand off to lee for follow-up RCAs and to coordinate remediation tickets. @lee you'll own the postmortem write-up.

lee: acknowledged. I'll open JIRA for root cause, one for retry config roll-forward, and one for cache/TLC improvements.

cs_triage_bot: closing customer comms loop: 3 customers currently awaiting update. Next update scheduled in 25m.

sre_oncall: wrapping up active mitigation — cache-flag remains enabled, auth scaled, retry_policy rolled back. Metrics stable. Dropping to monitoring-only mode. If error rate creeps up, page immediately.

mike: adding retrospective action: add synthetic tests for org-lookup under cache miss to catch amplification scenarios.

nina: thanks team. Great quick coordination. :clap:

cs_triage_bot: incident severity: Sev3 (limited customer impact) — assigning follow-up owners.

lee: creating the postmortem doc and will link back here. Closing thread in 40m unless further alerts.

incident-bot: Incident log appended: incident-id=INC-20260315-1746 severity=3 mitigated=true

sre_oncall: Thanks everyone. I'll hand to oncall follow-up. Leaving notes in casebook. :white_check_mark:
